findings_to_judge.finding: Navan's Q2 FY27 revenue guide of $219-221m is flat sequentially on Q1's $220m, but the company's only observable prior year grew +9.6% sequentially over the same fiscal quarters (Q1 FY26 $157.1m -> Q2 FY26 $172.2m, derivable from the disclosed 9M FY26 revenue of $524.3m less Q3 FY26 of $195m, and cross-checked by the stated 40% and 28% YoY growth rates); consensus of $220.5m is the guide midpoint to within $0.5m, so the street has not applied that seasonality at all.

The price half of Navan's gross bookings accelerated sharply across its fiscal Q2 (May-Jul 2026): US CPI airline fares ran +26.7%, +26.5% and +25.5% YoY in May/Jun/Jul against +7.1%, +14.9% and +20.7% in Feb/Mar/Apr, its fiscal Q1 -- roughly a 12pp step-up -- while consensus gross bookings of $2.86bn implies a 7.7% sequential DECLINE from Q1's $3.1bn, versus a roughly +1% sequential move in the same fiscal quarters a year earlier.

The 12% drawdown from the 2026-08-27 all-time high is at least partly mechanical post-lock-up insider supply, not a fundamental de-rating: CEO Ariel Cohen sold 168,378 shares directly plus 75,000 through each of three GST trusts at $30.1441 on 08-27 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-01-06, alongside a cluster of five Form 4s filed 08-24 and four Form 144s filed 08-27.

US airline-fare CPI averaged +26.2% y/y across May-July 2026 (Navan's fiscal Q2) versus +14.2% y/y across Feb-April 2026 (fiscal Q1), and the seasonally-adjusted index rose 6.4% sequentially between those two windows (291.3 avg to 310.0 avg) — a ~12pp step-up in the dollar-price tailwind to gross booking volume inside the quarter management guided to 28% revenue growth, down 12pp from Q1's 40%.

Navan's Q2 FY27 guide of $219-221m implies exactly 0% sequential revenue growth off Q1's $220m, whereas the same fiscal quarter a year earlier grew +9.1% sequentially ($157.5m to $171.9m); repeating last year's own seasonality would put Q2 at roughly $240m, i.e. +40% y/y — the same growth rate Navan just printed — against a guide of +28%.

CEO Ariel Cohen sold 393,378 shares at $30.1441 on 2026-08-27 — 168,378 personally plus 75,000 from each of three GST trusts, all three of which went to zero holdings — nine trading sessions before the print, and Lightspeed entities distributed roughly 2.5m shares in June at $19-20 and continued trimming in July.
